title: Sticky route state causing wrong model selection after capacity failover
creator: Liam Chen
description: After a capacity failover in us-east-1 on 2026-03-09, a subset of requests continued to be routed to an outdated model variant because a sticky routing state (route affinity + policy cache) persisted across the failover. This caused elevated latency for affected customers and a small increase in error retries as requests hit a heavier variant not provisioned in the target pool. This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigations applied, and permanent action items to prevent recurrence.
investigation_findings: Root cause: policy evaluation cache in the routing control plane was not invalidated when the capacity failover moved traffic; cache entries contained a stale variant_preference bit that forced selection of an incompatible variant.
Sticky affinity: an internal sticky-route token stored in Redis persisted across the node replacement sequence; sticky TTLs were long (15m) and were not revoked by the failover controller.

Race window: control plane issued a region-level failover and then re-registered capacity; during registration, the policy version header used by the serving runtime did not increment, so serving nodes accepted cached policy decisions.

Observable effects: 0.4% spike in p99 latency for affected customer routes, 2x increase in model selection errors for a small traffic segment, and repeated variant fetches that increased cross-region egress during retries.

Existing mitigations: immediate hotfix invalidated route cache entries for failing pools and shortened sticky-route TTL to 30s for the emergency window; traffic was gradually drained from the older variant and a temporary rule enforced model-compatible fallbacks.
Why this differed from previous routing incidents: not a routing loop; failure mode was stale state + sticky affinity persisting post-failover rather than policy graph corruption.
timeline: 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC: Autoscaler initiated capacity failover in us-east-1 due to thermal event on a GPU rack.
2026-03-09 03:18 UTC: Serving nodes re-registered, control plane reported successful failover; monitoring showed a small p99 latency bump.
2026-03-09 03:25 UTC: On-call noticed model selection mismatch alerts for 3 customer routes — analysis began.
2026-03-09 03:40 UTC: Emergency hotfix deployed: route cache invalidation targeted to affected pools and sticky TTL reduced to 30s.
2026-03-09 04:05 UTC: Metrics normalized; incident declared mitigated. Post-incident investigation started.
2026-03-11: Deeper code review identified missing cache-invalidation hook in failover controller and lack of policy-version bump on registration.
2026-03-13: Drafted action items and prioritization; assigned engineering owners.
2026-03-14: This ticket created to track long-term fixes and instrumentation work.
action_items: Add an explicit route-cache invalidation step to the failover controller: on any region capacity movement, invalidate policy caches and sticky tokens for affected pools (owner: platform/failover team, estimate 5).

Introduce a monotonically-incremented policy_version header emitted by the control plane during any config change or registration; serving runtime must reject cached decisions older than current policy_version (owner: routing-service, estimate 8).
Reduce default sticky-route TTL from 15m to 2m and make it configurable per-customer; create an emergency mode that temporarily shrinks TTL on failover (owner: routing-service, estimate 3).
Add an automated e2e test that simulates node replacement + capacity failover and verifies policy cache invalidation and correct model selection (owner: infra-test, estimate 5).
Create observability signals: gauge for stale-route-count, histogram for policy_version mismatches, and alert when stale-route-count > 0.1% of traffic for 5m (owner: observability, estimate 4).
Backfill per-request tracing to include policy_version, route_token_hash, and variant_selected so post-incident forensics are straightforward (owner: tracing-team, estimate 5).
Post-deploy runbook update: include explicit steps to force invalidation after a failover and verification queries for model-variant parity (owner: SRE, estimate 2).
Run a customer-impact audit to identify routes that experienced degraded latency and notify CS for outreach where appropriate (owner: CS-eng liaison, estimate 2).
Schedule a cross-team retro to review policy lifecycle and failover choreography with runtime, routing, and failover controller owners (owner: eng-manager, estimate 1).

Consider a future change: make routing decisions idempotent by encoding variant compatibility in the request signature so serving nodes can refuse incompatible cached choices (owner: architecture, estimate 13).
notes: We intentionally limited the emergency change surface to cache invalidation and TTL reduction to avoid risking wider rollout disruption.
Prior incident patterns suggested loops and policy-graph bugs; this one is a state-staleness class and requires different guardrails (cache + versioning).
Next milestone: land policy_version and failover-cache hook in runtime-1.22 branch, target deploy in runtime-1.22.1.
If any action item slips beyond the due_date, escalate to the eng leadership triage list and add a customer comms plan.
